top_choice_rationale: P001 (Mircea Cărtărescu, citation scoped to the prose project with poetry only as foundation) remains the most complete case on the common criteria. The voice is distinctive. Memory, the body and dream appear to be the structural principle of very large books such as the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid, so formal ambition and imaginative depth look like one thing. The project seems cumulative across volumes, which bears on sustained quality. This rests on public knowledge and the supplied descriptions, none independently verified. It is conditional on two open points: whether the late long books are evenly sustained, and how much density and rhythm survive translation. I rank Adonis (P002) second because his remaking of Arabic poetic language is a clearly documented linguistic achievement, and Carson (P003) third because her English text is directly legible to the committee, though a text-only citation can name only part of her invention. All three are serious candidates and translation uncertainty applies to each, so I rank P000 last. The evidence is not so thin that no award is warranted, and this ordering reflects weighting judgments, not demonstrated superiority. Shared support among colleagues is not part of the reasoning.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. The profile records no personal, professional or archival tie to any shortlisted writer. Recorded only as context: I was elected alongside Steve Sem-Sandberg in 2020, am married to Pär Nuder, and my Nobel biography drew on Nobel Foundation and family archives. My background in non-fiction is not evidence of preference. Whether a co-opted member votes is undocumented, so this vote is a modeling assumption.
